name: Baroda Extrusion Ltd
title: Baroda Extrusion Ltd - 513502 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Baroda Extrusion Q1 FY27 revenue rose to ₹47.90 crore (vs ₹38.05 crore) and PAT to ₹2.64 crore, with a ₹20 crore order book as of 31 July 2026.
summary.overview: Management presented Q1 FY27 against the prior-year quarter, with revenue up about 26% YoY and EBITDA up about 238% to ₹3.68 crore. The company is described as virtually debt-free and cash profitable, and is considering a heavy-capacity hydraulic extrusion press with a stated capex of ₹20-25 crore. Management guided to 35-40% growth for FY27/FY28 but gave no formal numeric guidance. The call was largely qualitative, and several figures were stated inconsistently (the speaker quoted FY25/FY26 labels for Q1 FY27 numbers and gave monthly volume figures that conflicted).

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹38.05 crore in Q1 FY26; +25.87% YoY
vs 2.86% in prior-year quarter (as read out by moderator)

segments.name: Copper and copper alloy products (solid, hollow, sections, nuggets)
segments.commentary: Management cited a sales run-rate of about 150-160 tons per month in one answer and about 430 tons per quarter (~145 tons per month, including job work) in another; these figures are inconsistent. Job work and trading are included in the mix.

segments.name: Ancillary job work and trading
segments.commentary: Company does forging, machining and trading of copper sheet alongside its own production; trading contributed higher income in one recent period, per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects 35-40% minimum growth for FY27 and FY28 versus the prior year; one answer also cited about 25% already achieved.
EBITDA margin expected to hold, varying by about 1-2% either way, per management.
Capex of ₹20-25 crore for a heavy-capacity hydraulic extrusion press and other machines; post-expansion capacity stated as about 500 tons per month (~6,000 tons per annum), with both plants running.
Management aspires to ₹1,000 crore revenue in 3-5 years and referred to ₹2,000 crore in a later answer; current revenue base is described as about ₹200 crore annualised.
Management said it can accept about 50% more orders right now on existing machines, given limited capacity.
capex_capacity: Heavy-capacity hydraulic extrusion press under evaluation; capex stated at ₹20-25 crore including machines and plant and machinery.
Expansion planned adjacent to the running factory in Vadodara on existing land, to avoid disruption.
Company has 20 drawbenches and extrusion capacity; machines were upgraded, per management.
Management indicated the company was 'a bit late' on expansion after not expanding major capacity for about 35 years.
demand_pricing: Demand drivers cited: electrical infrastructure, transformers, switchgear, data centres, EVs, renewables and power equipment.
Exports: a customer makes copper strips for the US market, where duties have reportedly fallen; export orders are also rising domestically.
Defence: supplies via GeM tenders and to ancillary vendors; large-OD copper pipes for ammunition applications are under development, with no regular volume yet.
Pricing: company does not hedge; it buys raw material against orders and uses LME/BME-linked customer contracts to protect margins.
Customers include BARC and NPCIL-linked government companies for oxygen-free forged and machined components, sourced via GeM; the company says this is currently a minor share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from BARC and NPCIL, and what products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it supplies oxygen-free material and forged/machined components via GeM, with a minor current share; expansion of heavy presses is expected to capture more volume.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on revenue and EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of 35-40% minimum versus last year, with about 25% already achieved, and margins expected to hold within 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue increase from the ₹25-30 crore infrastructure investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-expansion, capacity to be above 500 tons per month (about 6,000 tons per annum), with heavy sizes and low-weight items produced at the new unit.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company capture import substitution across EV, renewables, power and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it already supplies major Indian customers for pipes, flats, rods and bolts, has drawing capacity, and that market is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the margin improvement and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to rising demand, cost control, an integrated team and some higher trading income in an earlier period; it expects margins to be consistent.

qa_highlights.question: How to reach ₹1,000 crore in 3 years and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is ₹20-25 crore; management believes the target is achievable in 3-5 years, with volume and margin both expected to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Monthly volume and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Answers were inconsistent: 120 tons/month implied by ₹200 crore annual revenue, 145 tons/month average, and 430 tons per quarter; management said machine efficiency is below installed capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Open to inorganic growth or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to deals that fit its industry, including production tie-ups, but has no plans for a takeover and will not take financial risk beyond capacity.

risks_watch: Figures are inconsistent across the call (quarterly vs monthly volumes, FY25/FY26 labels for Q1 FY27 numbers); verify against the filed results.
No formal guidance; the 35-40% growth and 1,000-2,000 crore targets are management aspirations without a stated timeline or funding plan beyond ₹20-25 crore capex.
No hedging policy: raw-material price volatility can affect inventory and margins, although management says customer pricing is linked to LME/BME.
Dependence on a small number of large customers and on government/defence orders via GeM, which are not regular in volume yet.
Expansion execution: new press commissioning timeline not given; the company says it has been capacity-constrained for years and carries an operating history of lapses.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the long-term story, but vague and unstructured on numbers, with frequent restatements. Evasive on the share price and valuation question, which was answered only in general terms about integrity and shareholder returns.
key_quotes: Our object is not simply to increase capacity. Our objective is to create profitable capacity, increase value addition, and build sustainable long-term growth.
The margins are always low, right? So, we have a fixed setup near in Vadodara, we have office here, we have a very integrated team.

adds.what: Heavy-capacity hydraulic extrusion press and other machines, capex ₹20-25 crore; post-expansion capacity ~500 t/month (~6,000 tpa)

growth.why: Management guides to a minimum 35-40% rise for FY27-28 (midpoint 37.5%) and says it can take ~50% more orders on existing machines, with a ₹20 crore order book; but the press is only under evaluation with no timeline, and the call was qualitative with inconsistent figures.
